CAFETERIA LESSON · CAFETERIA · AGES 2–5 YEARS

French Fries — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson turns the tray’s most famous silhouette into a subtraction game — count the fries, eat one, count again.

What is this?

French fries are potatoes cut into sticks and fried or baked until golden. The card shows a white carton with fries standing at different heights — a little city skyline of potato.

What does it mean?

Count the fries and then count again after one disappears: that is subtraction in its tastiest form. The count that shrinks teaches more-than and less-than without any worksheet.

What does the child need to know?

Stand the fries upright for the count — a fry skyline counts better than a fry pile, and the different heights are part of the fun.

Why this matters

Fries are the food every child meets at every restaurant — attaching honest counting to them costs nothing and pays out all childhood.

What it teaches

Counting, take-away subtraction, and more-or-less comparison.

Words to learn

friescounttowerlessgonegolden

Say this to your child

“Stand them up — a fry city! Count the towers: one, two, three... Now eat one — crunch! How many now? Fewer! Again! One more gone... how many? The city shrinks!”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and count the standing fries — whatever number the picture gives. Then line up real fries like towers and count them. Eat one — loudly — and recount: how many now? Repeat until the skyline is gone, announcing the shrinking number each round. End by asking which had more: the first line or the last.

Look closer at the picture

Watch the recount: after eating, does the child recount from one or just announce the new number? Both are correct steps; recounting is the scaffolding, announcing is the growth.

Ask your child

How many fries now? Were there more before or after? Which is the tallest tower? What food are fries made from?

What your child can say or do

One less! / Three now. / More before! / Potato sticks!

Out in the real world

Fries arrive beside every restaurant kids’ meal — the disappearing count is the perfect pre-dinner game, played with the food itself.

Try it together

Fry skyline: build towers from standing fries on the plate, count each tower’s floors, then demolish city by city — one bite per floor. Demolish, count, repeat.

Understanding check

Line up three fries, eat one out of sight, and ask how many are left. Two — counted or announced — passes.

This lesson pairs with the French Fries flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Cafeteria.
